text: The MRI results showing disseminated white matter lesions, combined with your anemia and low white blood cell count, do not support a diagnosis of gastroenteritis. Can you tell me how long you have noticed these neurological symptoms and whether there is a history of multiple sclerosis or other autoimmune conditions?

speaker: Patient
text: 44-year-old male. The patient's daughter reports a 1-week history of right leg weakness, unsteady gait, and multiple falls. Over the past 6 months, the patient has been increasingly forgetful, losing his way on familiar routes and facing difficulties operating simple kitchen appliances. He has also been paranoid, agitated, and restless recently.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML). The clinical picture of rapidly progressive subcortical dementia, gait disturbance, and focal motor weakness in a middle-aged male, combined with disseminated non-enhancing white matter lesions on MRI and pancytopenia (specifically low lymphocytes), is highly characteristic of PML, likely due to an opportunistic infection in the setting of significant immunosuppression.
